value.statement: R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, m∈M and c,d∈K, the rule (t⊗c)(m⊗d)=tm⊗(cd) is well-defined on (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K and V_K=M⊗_ℤ K and defines a K-linear Lie action. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.
value.origin: problem.md:86-116; localization, induced Chevalley action and matrix units

patches.value: Choose m as in F001. Apply M002 with R₀=ℤ, A=M, S₀=R and the integer basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_(i∈I) of M_R. The map ι_M sends these basis vectors to m_i; a finite R-linear relation among their images is also a complex-linear relation, so all coefficients are zero. Thus ι_M is injective, identifies M_R with the R-span of the m_i inside V, and its complex span is V. For any r≥0, admissibility H004 and D005 imply X(r)M⊂M and Y(r)M⊂M; R-linearity gives preservation of M_R. In particular X(1)=x and Y(1)=y preserve M; H002 gives h=xy−yx on V, so h preserves M as well. The commutators in H002 show directly that the integer span of x,y,h is bracket-closed, since all three structure constants are integers. For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh and m∈M the restriction tm is in M. The rule (t⊗c)(m⊗d)=tm⊗(cd), c,d∈K, respects addition and both integer balancing relations, hence defines a K-bilinear action on the two tensor products. Its Lie representation identity is verified on pure tensors by the identity in the given complex Lie module V, and then on finite sums by bilinearity. Thus it is the asserted induced Lie action, without identifying the Chevalley integer form with any different reduction.
